title: #004. General Product Mix (m x n Matrix)
subtitle: Generalize the two-product creamery into matrix form across arbitrary numbers of products and shared resources.
markdown:
# #004. General Product Mix (m x n Matrix)

<!-- section:scenario -->
Now let's generalize **#002** from two fixed products to any number of products $n$ and shared capacities $m$.

An artisan creamery manufactures $n$ flavors of bulk gelato (sold by the liter as **continuous** non-negative quantities `quantities[j] >= 0`). Each batch is constrained by $m$ shared ingredients and kitchen capacities `capacities[k]`, where producing 1 liter of flavor $j$ consumes `usages[k][j]` units of resource $k$ and yields unit profit `margins[j]`. Determine how many liters of each flavor to produce in order to **maximize total profit**.

<!-- section:io -->
- **Input (`P004Input`)**:
  - `margins: number[]` — profit per unit of product $j$ ($0 \le j < n$)
  - `usages: number[][]` — resource matrix where `usages[k][j]` is resource $k$ required per unit of product $j$
  - `capacities: number[]` — available capacity of each resource $k$ ($0 \le k < m$)
- **Output (`P004Output`)**:
  - `quantities: number[]` — non-negative continuous production amounts of length $n$
  - `totalProfit: number` — maximized profit $\sum_j \text{margins}[j] \cdot \text{quantities}[j]$

<!-- section:example -->
Suppose flavor 0 earns `500`/L (using `3` milk, `1` sugar) and flavor 1 earns `300`/L (using `1` milk, `2` sugar), with `90` milk and `80` sugar available:

- **Greedy temptation**: Prioritize only flavor 0 because its `500`/L margin is higher. Milk caps flavor 0 at `90 / 3 = 30` L, leaving `50` sugar unused for a profit of only **`15,000`**.
- **Optimal LP blend**: Producing `quantities = [20, 30]` uses all `90` milk and `80` sugar simultaneously for **`19,000`** profit — `4,000` higher than greedy!

<!-- section:hint1 -->
The decision variables `quantities` are already declared in the starter code. Loop over every resource index `k` from `0` to `capacities.length - 1` and add `dot(usages[k], quantities) <= capacities[k]`.

<!-- section:hint2 -->
Add `` m.objective(maximize(expr`dot(${input.margins}, ${quantities})`)) `` (or `h.maximize(...)` in Python), solve, and return `{ quantities, totalProfit }` without rounding continuous liter volumes to integers (`Case 2` has fractional vertex `[6.666..., 46.666..., 0]`).

<!-- section:formulation -->
$$
\begin{aligned}
\max \quad & \sum_{j=0}^{n-1} c_j x_j \\
\text{s.t.} \quad & \sum_{j=0}^{n-1} a_{k,j} x_j \le b_k && \forall k \in \{0, \dots, m-1\} \\
& x_j \ge 0 && \forall j \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}
\end{aligned}
$$

judge.m0: Output must be an object { quantities, totalProfit }.
judge.m3: Reported totalProfit ({p0}) does not match computed margin sum ({p1}).
judge.m4: Feasible production plan, but profit ({p0}) is below the LP optimum ({p1}).
